document.title: Manipulation Frames and Handle Targets
document.purpose: Record where manipulation frames and handle hit-target detection live after adding rotate and size mode handles.

summary: Direct manipulation displays manipulation frames for the current selection. Rotate handles and size handles are controlled by workspace manipulation state, not command modes. Handles are visible and tokenized as targets without adding the old move-object command, secondary-button drag, full-world snapshots, or new world revisions for showing handles.

commands.rotate: The rotate handle is shown when workspace.manipulation.kind is rotate.
commands.size: Size handles are shown when workspace.manipulation.kind is size.

policy: Exactly one selected node uses that node's world bounds.
Multiple selected nodes use the axis-aligned union of selected node world bounds.
Rotated rectangles use transformed corner bounds from rect_points_world(node).
Circles and ellipses use x/y/w/h bounds.
Unknown node kinds return no bounds and are ignored by selected_bounds_world().
Handles are projected in screen space from the selected world bounds.
Rotate manipulation creates one circular rotate handle above the top-center of the frame.
Size manipulation creates square corner handles named nw, ne, sw, and se.
Projection draws frames only when the selection is non-empty and workspace manipulation state is visible.
Projection draws canvas items tagged manipulation.
Projection reads workspace and world state but does not mutate semantic state or world state.
Handle hit-testing happens during target tokenization.
Handle hit-testing uses screen-space hit rectangles around projected handle specs.
Handles are checked before node picking so handle targets win over underlying nodes.

node.node_id: selected node id under the pointer

handle.handle_name: rotate, nw, ne, sw, or se

notes: handle:rotate and handle:size are used by handle transformation organisms for resource coordination.
No world mutation resources are claimed by handle detection.

remaining-work: Better handle styling and cursor feedback.
